newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Canadian Airlines eyes Shanghai flights.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Airlines eyes Shanghai flights.

text.p: Canadian Airlines International Limited says it hopes to restart flying to Shanghai "within the next 12 months" as part of its drive to increase services to Asia.

Tony Buckley, the airline's regional director for Asia also said CAI is doubling its Boeing 767 service between Vancouver and the Chinese capital Beijing to four flights a week because of rising demand.

Canadian's winter schedule which begins next month also sees more trans-Pacific flights to Hong Kong -- nine non-stops a week from Vancouver compared to seven last winter. There will also be six flights weekly to Taipei with two services continuing onto Kuala Lumpur in a code-share arrangement with Malaysia Airlines.
CAI has also begun a code-share alliance with Philippine Airlines between Manila and Vancouver which began on September 19.

CAI say the 21 percent increase in services to its eight direct destinations in Asia from next month will also boost air cargo carrying capacity as aircraft are switched from unprofitable European routes to its growing market in the Far East.
"China is our future and so is Asia," said. Buckley who's based in Hong Kong.

"We'd certainly like to get back into Shanghai as soon as we can. If we can get some airplanes from somewhere else we will. We can start in a month or two, but in reality I would say we will be flying there in the next 12 months," he added.
Canada's only carrier to China -- which first gained rights 47 years ago this month -- stopped flying to Shanghai last year because of a slump in demand, but this has now recovered.

CAI say the new service would be a dedicated flight unlike its previous routing via Beijing. CAI flights to Beijing were restarted three years ago after a big slump in demand in the wake of Tiannamen Square.
He said discussions have been held to make it easier for Chinese nationals to visit Canada. Vancouver airport is not a transfer airport and a visa is required to connect onto US destinations.

"We can build up Shanghai a lot faster if there were no visa requirement or there was a visa office in Shanghai. There have been a number of discussions to overcome this because everyone is very anxious to see Canadian fly out of Shanghai," Buckley said.

"The 767 is a tremendous aircraft for a developmental market and gives us the ability to offer increased frequencies for business travellers and carry a lot of traffic from China through Canada to the United States where we are expanding rapidly," Buckley said. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
